description: §4.12.5 — a nested `<program name= lang=>` is a FOREIGN LANGUAGE SIDECAR, whether or not it also declares `port=`. It emits no `new Worker(...)` and no worker bundle. Pre-fix (S356) the §23.4 carve-out that suppressed the bogus worker keyed on `port=` ALONE, so this `port=`-less spelling of the same execution context was still compiled as a §4.12.4 web worker and shipped a 24-byte stub bundle. The declaration deliberately does NOT fire E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL: §23.4 already fails the sidecar closed at the `use foreign:name { … }` site with E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL, and two errors on one unbuilt shape is two diagnostics for one mistake.
rationale: §4.12.3's table gives "Foreign language sidecar | `name=`, `lang=` (non-WASM language) | Subprocess with HTTP/socket" — `port=` is a sidecar CONFIGURATION attribute (§4.12.2: "Port number for sidecar HTTP/socket communication"), not the discriminator. §4.12.3 normative (S356): the inline-worker context is selected if and only if `name=` is present and `lang=`/`mode=`/`route=`/`db=`/`port=` are all absent. The absence of a declaration-site diagnostic here is the deliberate carve-out recorded in the §34 row for E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL.
